summary: Shuichi Maida (1906–1967) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Kyoto University and under Haya Akegarasu.
Shuichi Nara (b. 1961) works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Keio University and held posts at Chuo University and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 2026).

Shuji Takayama is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Ryukoku University and Bukkyo University (attested 2003), as well as Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College and Musashino University (attested 2006).

Shujiro Shimada (1907–1994) was a scholar in Japanology, Sinology, and history and archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1928–1931) and served on the faculty at Princeton University (~1962–1976).

Shujun Motegi (b. 1951) specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi at Banaras Hindu University (1973–1975) and earned an MA from Kyoto University (1977), later serving as Professor of Ethics at Shinshu University (attested 2010).

Shuken Ito (b. 1947) is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral studies at Komazawa University, subsequently serving there as assistant, lecturer, associate professor, and professor between ~1973 and 1991, and visiting professor at Aichi Gakuin University (1998).
Shuman Chen is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. Chen studied under traditional teacher Weijue Shi and completed a PhD at Northwestern University under doctoral supervisor Brook Ziporyn.

Shuming Liang (1893–1988) worked in philosophy, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Shuntian Middle School, he joined Peking University's philosophy department in 1917 and later founded the Shandong Rural Reconstruction Institute and the China Democratic League.

Shumpei Ueyama (1921–2012) worked in philosophy, Japanology, and history/archaeology. A Kyoto University graduate, he taught there as associate professor (1954) and professor (1968), later serving as president of Kyoto City University of Arts (~1986–1989) and director of Kyoto National Museum (~1988–1995).
Shun Hidaka is a scholar of Buddhist studies who held a research post at the Buddhist Art Resource Center in 2012 and a part-time lecturer post at Otani University (attested 2014).

Shun'ei Hirai (b. 1930) is a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Komazawa University as lecturer (1964), professor (from 1970), vice president (1986), and emeritus professor (2001).
Shun'ei Mori is a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied under Shoko Takeuchi. Mori held appointments at Ryukoku University (attested 1990) and Chikushi Jogakuen Junior College (attested 1995).
Shunei Tsuboi (1923–2010) was a scholar in Buddhist studies who served as a professor at Bukkyo University (attested 1963 and 1972).

Shunji Hosaka (b. 1956), a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and Buddhist studies, studied at Waseda University (~1976–1980). He held posts at Reitaku University (~1991–2004), Chuo University (~2004–2021), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies, and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Shunkyo Katsumata (1909–1994) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1932–1935). He held posts at Toyo University and Taisho University (~1944–1982), where he became emeritus professor.
Shunpaku Nakao is a scholar of Buddhist studies who served at Shuchiin University as associate professor (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1976).

Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Sōkō-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center (1962) and Tassajara Zen Mountain Center (1967).

Shunsho Manabe (1939–2021) specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1958–1963) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University (~1993–2010), where he was a professor.
Shunsho Terakawa (1928–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1951–1954) and served as a faculty member and emeritus professor at Otani University (~1966–2000).
Shuntaro Kondo (b. 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned a PhD from Ryukoku University in 2011 and worked there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2012).
